propositions: The `[operator-attested]` tag is renamed to `[non-codebase]` as the canonical form, while `[operator-attested]` is retained as an undocumented backward-compatibility alias to avoid reclassifying 827 immutable event-sourced tickets.

The canonical regex matcher must accept both `[non-codebase]` and `[operator-attested]` case-insensitively using a non-capturing alternation to preserve `findall()` arity and avoid breaking enrichment.

The deterministic matcher and LLM emitters are synchronized so `completion_verifier.md`, `contracts.py`, `completion_verdict.schema.json`, and both `criteria_routing.json` files (trigger and vocabulary) are widened in lockstep.
Author-facing documentation emits `[non-codebase]` only; `[operator-attested]` does not appear in documented surfaces, enforced by negative tests on the packaged guide.
Legacy `kind: "operator-attested"` verdicts in the audit system must render identically to new `kind: "non-codebase"` verdicts via reader-side widening before emitter changes.
The new tag name resists attestation-laundering by construction: an author cannot credibly claim codebase file paths are non-codebase evidence.
